subject: Science
title: A simple genetic cross
objective_verbatim: Complete a genetic cross (digital Punnett square).
reading_age_est: rough ARI grade 4.84 on 956 pupil-visible words; heuristic age guide 10.84 years, not a formal reading-age test
pupil_words: I am learning to calculate genetic probability with a Punnett square and evaluate its limits.
success_criteria: I can pair one allele from each parent.
I can find the aa chance in four squares.
I can evaluate why probability does not guarantee an exact count.

vocab.example: A and a represent two alleles in our invented model.

vocab.definition: the pair of alleles shown by letters
vocab.example: Aa is one possible genotype in this model.

vocab.definition: an allele shown by one copy in this simple model
vocab.example: A is dominant in our invented flower model.

vocab.definition: an allele shown when two copies are present in this model
vocab.example: aa shows the recessive version in our model.

vocab.definition: a grid that shows possible allele pairs
vocab.example: The Punnett square for Aa × aa has four cells.

worked_example.full: Place A/a atop the grid for one parent; place a/a at its side for the other. Pair one allele from each edge: Aa, aa, Aa, aa. Two of four boxes are aa: a 1 in 2 chance per offspring, not an exact family count.
worked_example.faded: Aa × aa: top A, a; side a, a. First row Aa, aa; second row ___, ___. Chance of aa: ___ out of 4.
worked_example.removed_step: Combine one top allele and one side allele in each second-row square; count two aa squares.
worked_example.fade_next: Next lesson hide the top A/a headings; pupil selects them from the parent genotype before filling the grid.

cfu.question: Show me: which allele can the aa parent pass on?

hinge.question: New cross: Aa × Aa. What is the chance of aa for each offspring?

options.diagnosis: Counts the two heterozygous squares rather than the one aa square.
Counts all outcomes except aa rather than the recessive genotype.

options.text: D. Certain for every single offspring.
options.diagnosis: Treats one possible aa square as a guaranteed outcome.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more right → move on. Otherwise re-model the Aa × aa top and side headings with two colours, pair one allele in each square, then ask the parallel hinge. No automatic mark or saved response.
hinge.parallel_hinge: Third cross: AA × aa. What is the chance of Aa for each offspring? Answer: certain; every possible pair contains one A and one a. This does not set an exact family size.

misconceptions.misconception: A possible aa outcome is certain for every offspring.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses D, making the aa outcome certain.
misconceptions.correction: Each offspring has one chance in four in the model; it is not guaranteed.

misconceptions.misconception: The two Aa cells in a cross count as aa.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses B, counting Aa squares as aa.
misconceptions.correction: Read the two allele symbols in each square; only one square is aa.

we_do.support: Place one letter tile from the top and one from the side into a single square. Point to the next pair.
we_do.stretch: Predict the aa chance for Aa × Aa before checking a second model. Explain the change.

tiers.F: Complete Aa × aa with allele tiles.
tiers.M: Calculate and justify the aa probability from the grid.
tiers.H: Evaluate an exact-count claim about four real offspring.

stems.M: I count ___ aa squares out of four, so …
stems.H: The grid shows a chance, not a promise, because …

tiers.go_deeper: Compare aa chances for Aa × Aa and Aa × aa with a second grid.
tiers.early_finisher: Correct a faulty grid that gives an Aa parent two A headings; explain its wrong probability.

adaptations.cognition_learning: Keep the four-cell allele model in view; remove one cue for We do, then ask pupils to repeat a fresh example without it.
adaptations.communication_interaction: Offer the key word card and a private partner turn before speaking to the group; accept point, sign or AAC.
adaptations.semh: Check in before the top question and hinge; offer a private first answer, agreed pause and one-step return.
adaptations.sensory_physical: Provide an enlarged high-contrast model and keyboard focus; allow speech-to-text or exact scribing.
adaptations.eal: Pre-teach defined science words with examples; let pupils plan in any language while keeping M/H reasoning open.

speaking_frames: One allele from the top is …; one from the side is …; together they make …
The chance is … because …; this does not promise …

ta_focus.i_do: “Watch one letter from each parent enter one square.”
ta_focus.we_do: “Which edge has not supplied a letter yet?”
ta_focus.independent: “Point to one finished square. How will you use that step next?”

prompt_ladder: Wait five seconds for an independent tile move.
Point to the unfinished square and the two edges.
Ask “Which one allele can this parent pass on?”
Model one edge-to-square move; pupil repeats with another square.
Complete one square together, then pupil tries a fresh one alone.

F.q: What can the aa parent pass on?
How many cells are in a two-by-two grid?

M.a: The a from the Aa parent can pair with either a from the aa parent.

M.q: What chance does two out of four represent?
M.a: One in two for each offspring in this model.

H.q: Why is a probability not a fixed count in four offspring?
H.a: Each offspring is a separate chance; the grid gives possible proportions.
The aa chance becomes one in four in the simple model.

diagrams.caption: Invented A/a flower model: Aa × aa gives two Aa and two aa possibilities. Each square is a possibility, not a family count. Simplified.
